retraction.what_is_retracted: Round 56x claim: 'No device addresses clot-VESSEL adhesion. F2 = completely unsolved.'
retraction.why_retracted: US11504151B2 (Stryker Corporation) describes an expandable scraper that explicitly dislodges clot material from the vessel wall with controlled radial force. Claim 1 covers: expandable braided basket → expand against vessel walls → pull proximally to 'remove or dislodge the clot material from the vessel wall.' This DIRECTLY addresses clot-vessel adhesion as a physical mechanism.
retraction.corrected_classification: F2 = KNOWN physical failure mode; current mitigation EXISTS (scraping via US11504151B2), but residual failure/measurement/control gap is UNKNOWN.

us11504151b2_analysis.title: Thrombectomy apparatuses (expandable scraper)
claim_1_elements: Elongate shaft with flexible inner/outer members
Basket deforms from unexpanded to expanded configuration
Lock forms loop to decrease effective length
what_it_does: Pulls proximally to SCRAPE clot from vessel wall
'remove or dislodge the clot material from the vessel wall'
Controlled radial force against vessel walls
Non-uniform radial force for 'gentle and effective scraping'
what_it_does_NOT_do: Does NOT MEASURE adhesion before scraping (no sensing)
Does NOT SELECT retrieval strategy based on adhesion state (no closed-loop selection)
Does NOT CHARACTERIZE clot-wall interaction before first pass
Does NOT control scraping force based on real-time feedback (force is PRE-SET)

layer_A_sensing.description: Determine adhesion/attachment state before or during first pass
prior_art: EP4637580A1: force sensor measuring pulling force on thrombus (TOTAL force, not adhesion-specific)
US20140018665A1: compressable catheter tip with image-based force sensing
US20260000423A1 (2026): sensor feedback to controller for device control
layer_A_sensing.assessment: PARTIALLY OCCUPIED — force sensing at catheter tip EXISTS, but total pulling force ≠ clot-vessel adhesion specifically. The question of whether adhesion can be ISOLATED from total force is UNKNOWN.
layer_A_sensing.ce_012: PARTIALLY PASSES — measuring total force is existing; isolating adhesion as a distinct component may be new
layer_A_sensing.ce_013: PASSES — adhesion is causally independent of existing measurements
layer_A_sensing.ce_014: APPLIED — 10 searches, 25 patents, none specifically for adhesion isolation/decomposition

layer_B_intervention.description: Locally reduce attachment without damaging vessel
prior_art: US11504151B2: expandable scraper that dislodges clot from vessel wall
layer_B_intervention.assessment: MATERIALLY OCCUPIED — scraping/dislodging from vessel wall is explicitly claimed
layer_B_intervention.verdict: Layer B is NOT a viable invention direction

layer_C_closed_loop_selection.description: Determine which physical retrieval strategy to deploy based on measured state
prior_art: US20260000423A1: sensor feedback for device control (same-device adjustment, not strategy selection)
layer_C_closed_loop_selection.assessment: PARTIALLY OCCUPIED — closed-loop device control exists, but selecting BETWEEN different strategies (scraper vs aspiration vs stent retriever) based on measured adhesion does NOT
layer_C_closed_loop_selection.ce_012: UNCERTAIN — depends on whether strategy selection produces a new technical effect

narrowest_surviving_gap.question: Can clot-VESSEL adhesion be ISOLATED and measured as a DISTINCT component of retrieval resistance (not just total pulling force), and does this SPECIFIC measurement change which retrieval strategy the clinician selects (not just adjust the same device)?
requires: 1. A method to DECOMPOSE total retrieval force into components (adhesion vs friction vs drag vs clot-cohesion)
2. A decision rule that maps adhesion level to strategy selection (e.g., high adhesion → scraper, low adhesion → aspiration)
3. Evidence that this decomposition + selection improves outcomes
narrowest_surviving_gap.ce_015_needed: Can adhesion be isolated from total force? Total force = adhesion + friction + drag + clot-clot cohesion. Can these be separated by measurement characteristics (e.g., adhesion has different force profile than friction)? This is a PHYSICS question requiring calculation.
narrowest_surviving_gap.adhesion_force_range: 0.01-0.1 N (MCA), up to 0.7 N (prolonged interaction per rabbit data)

vocabulary_used: clot adhesion force measurement catheter sensor
ce_014_deep_patent_search.no_patent_found_for: Isolating clot-vessel adhesion as a distinct component of retrieval resistance for strategy selection

verdict.narrowest_gap_identified: Adhesion isolation from total force + strategy selection
verdict.classification: DISCOVERY HYPOTHESIS — NOT promoted. The narrowest gap (adhesion isolation + strategy selection) passes CE-013 and partially passes CE-012/CE-014, but CE-015 (physics authority) is NOT yet applied and the §103 risk from combining existing force sensing + existing strategy options is UNCERTAIN.
next_steps: 1. CE-015: Calculate whether adhesion can be PHYSICALLY ISOLATED from total retrieval force (different force profiles, measurement signatures, or temporal patterns)
2. Article XX: Does the inability to isolate adhesion actually cause clinical failure? (Or do clinicians already compensate by trying different strategies?)
3. Full 12-stage patent attack on 'force decomposition for strategy selection in thrombectomy'
4. Decision-value: would knowing adhesion level change which device clinicians use FIRST? (vs current trial-and-error approach)
5. §103 assessment: combining force sensing (EP4637580A1) + strategy selection (clinical judgment) + scraping (US11504151B2) — is this obvious?
